name: Kimura Disease

criteria.description: Presence of painless subcutaneous nodules or masses predominantly in head and neck region
Lymph node or lesion biopsy showing lymphoid follicular hyperplasia with eosinophilic infiltration and vascular proliferation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of painless subcutaneous mass with peripheral eosinophilia and characteristic histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on clinical presentation and histopathology; no universally accepted formal criteria exist.

laboratory: Proteinuria in cases with renal involvement
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing well-defined subcutaneous masses
MRI may reveal soft tissue involvement and vascular proliferation
other: Histopathology showing lymphoid follicular hyperplasia with eosinophilic infiltration and proliferation of postcapillary venules

distinguishingFeatures: Lesions are often painful or pruritic
Histology shows prominent vascular proliferation with histiocytes
Systemic symptoms such as night sweats and weight loss
Presence of Reed-Sternberg cells on biopsy

redFlags: Systemic symptoms such as unexplained weight loss or night sweats
Signs of renal impairment or nephrotic syndrome
references: Chen H, Thompson LD, Aguilera NS, Abbondanzo SL. Kimura disease: a clinicopathologic study of 21 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2004;28(4):505-513.
Kang HJ, Kim YD, Kim HJ, et al. Kimura disease: clinical and histopathological features. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol. 2010;24(6):678-682.
